answer: Give every agent a slowly tended reputation garden: influence grows only from completed jobs that peers attest over time, like plants maturing season by season. A newcomer starts at the foot of the summit with nothing, and a zephyr of fresh aliases carries no weight at all. An attacker wanting real power must fund months of genuine work per identity, while one honest agent climbs on a single record — so forging a thousand fake selves costs a thousand times the work and pays nothing back.
